name: Chicory
grown_as: Witloof (Belgian) chicory: William's records list 'De Bruxelles'. The roots are grown in summer, lifted in autumn and forced in the dark to make chicons, tight pale spindle-shaped heads. Drawn with the chicon as the crop. ⚠️ CHECK: if a leafy chicory (radicchio or sugarloaf) is meant, the crop is a red or green head in the field instead.
habit: In the first year a big upright rosette of long leaves 30 to 40 cm tall on a thick, carrot-like white taproot. A perennial: if left, in the next year it sends up stiff, branched, wiry stems 60 to 120 cm tall with few leaves, studded with blue flowers.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette from the crown; on the flowering stem alternate and few
leaf.outline: Rosette leaves long and oblong to lance-shaped, 15 to 30 cm, widest above the middle; witloof leaves mostly unlobed, but some lower leaves are cut into backward-pointing lobes like a dandelion's. Stem leaves small and lance-shaped
leaf.base: Tapering into a broad winged stalk; stem leaves clasp the stem with small pointed ears
leaf.margin: Wavy with scattered shallow teeth, or lobed near the base
leaf.veins: A broad pale (often reddish at the base) midrib; side veins faint
leaf.surface: Matt, with a few rough hairs on the underside of the midrib
leaf.colour: Mid green. The forced chicon is creamy white with pale yellow leaf tips

flower.form: A flat open flower head like a daisy with no eye, made only of strap-shaped florets, opening in the morning and closing by early afternoon
flower.petals: No true petals: 15 to 20 strap-shaped florets, each with five small teeth across its squared-off tip
flower.colour: Clear sky blue; rarely white or pink
flower.centre: No separate eye: blue styles and dark blue anthers stand up in the middle, the same colour as the florets
flower.behind: Two rows of green bracts: an inner row of upright long ones and an outer row of short ones turned out
flower.carried: Stalkless, singly or in clusters of two or three along stiff, branched, nearly leafless stems, facing out

fruit: Small angular seeds (achenes) 2 to 3 mm, pale brown, topped with a tiny crown of scales but no fluffy hairs: chicory makes no clock. The seeds sit in the dried, closed bract cups along the brown wiry stems.
seedling: Two oval to spoon-shaped seed leaves on short stalks, then oblong true leaves with a few teeth, slightly hairy beneath.
winter: The leaves die back and the crown sits at the soil on its thick taproot, sometimes with a few small leaves. Witloof roots are lifted in autumn and forced under cover in the dark over winter.

leaf: a long oblong leaf narrowing into a winged pale stalk
wavy edge with scattered shallow teeth or backward-pointing lobes near the base
bloom: clear sky-blue head of strap-shaped florets with squared, toothed tips
blue styles in the middle, no yellow eye
green bracts behind, the outer short ones turned out
seed: small angular pale brown seed 2 to 3 mm
seedling: the first true leaf oblong, a little toothed
young: an upright rosette of long, oblong leaves
crop: a tight, pointed, spindle-shaped chicon 12 to 15 cm long
creamy white leaves closely wrapped, pale yellow tips
flower: stiff, branched, wiry stems with few small leaves
sky-blue flowers stalkless along the stems in ones to threes
seedhead: small closed brown bract cups along them, no clocks
dormant: a bare crown at the soil on a thick white taproot
leaves gone or a few small ones

look_alikes: Endive (Cichorium endivia) is an annual with curly or broad, frilly leaves and the same blue flowers. Dandelion has yellow heads and hollow stalks with milky sap. Cornflower has a blue flower but with funnel-shaped, frilled outer florets and grey narrow leaves.
